facts.evidence: Reported revenue was $57.3 billion, while managed revenue (a non-GAAP measure) was $58.0 billion. Both reported and managed revenue increased 28% and 27%, respectively, compared to the second quarter of 2025.
Reported net income for the second quarter of 2026 was $21.2 billion, or $7.70 per share.
Net income excluding these significant items was $16.9 billion, or $6.14 per share. The release notes that results excluding significant items are non-GAAP financial measures.
Markets revenue surged 35% to $12.1 billion, driven by an 86% increase in Equity Markets revenue.
Return on tangible common equity (ROTCE), a non-GAAP measure, was 29% for the quarter. ROTCE excluding significant items was 23%.
This figure includes significant items: a $4.6 billion net gain related to Visa shares ($1.27 per share) and $1.0 billion in gains on certain equity investments ($0.29 per share).
The Firm declared a common dividend of $4.0 billion ($1.50 per share) and executed $6.2 billion in common stock net repurchases during the quarter.
Basel III common equity Tier 1 capital was $303 billion, resulting in a Standardized ratio of 14.1% and an Advanced ratio of 14.2%.

claims.claim: Reported net income for the second quarter of 2026 was $21.2 billion, or $7.70 per share.
Reported net income includes a significant item of a $4.6 billion net gain related to Visa shares, worth $1.27 per share.
Reported net income includes a significant item of $1.0 billion in gains on certain equity investments, worth $0.29 per share.
Net income excluding the significant items was $16.9 billion, or $6.14 per share.
The release notes that results excluding significant items are non-GAAP financial measures.
Reported revenue was $57.3 billion.
Managed revenue, a non-GAAP measure, was $58.0 billion.
Reported revenue increased 28% and managed revenue increased 27% compared with the second quarter of 2025.
Noninterest expense was $27.3 billion, up 15% from the prior-year period.
The reported overhead ratio was 48% and the managed (non-GAAP) overhead ratio was 47%.
ROTCE, a non-GAAP measure, was 29% for the quarter.
ROTCE excluding significant items was 23%.
CIB net income was $9.7 billion, up 46% year over year.
Markets revenue rose 35% to $12.1 billion.
The increase in Markets revenue was driven by an 86% increase in Equity Markets revenue.
Investment Banking fees rose 30% to $3.3 billion.
CIB total net revenue was $24.9 billion, up 27%.
CCB net income was $5.3 billion, up 3%.
Card Services & Auto net revenue grew 12% to $7.8 billion, supported by higher revolving balances.
The Card Services net charge-off rate was 3.34%.
Debit and credit card sales volume increased 10% year over year.
AWM net income was $2.0 billion, up 33%.
Assets under management reached $5.1 trillion, up 18% year over year.
AWM revenue increased 19% to $6.9 billion, driven by higher average market levels and strong net inflows of $50 billion in long-term AUM.
The release does not provide specific financial guidance or a quantitative outlook for future quarters.
Jamie Dimon said revenue in each line of business hit a new record.
Dimon cited elevated market activity and rigorous execution as key drivers.
Management noted the U.S. economy has shown resiliency with stronger business investment and hiring.
Management noted risks including geopolitical tensions, sticky inflation and large global fiscal deficits shifting below the surface.
Basel III common equity Tier 1 capital was $303 billion, with a Standardized ratio of 14.1% and an Advanced ratio of 14.2%.
Total Loss-Absorbing Capacity was $590 billion.
Average loans were $1.5 trillion.
Cash and marketable securities were $1.5 trillion.
The Firm declared a common dividend of $4.0 billion, or $1.50 per share.
The Firm executed $6.2 billion of common stock net repurchases during the quarter.
Noninterest expense growth of 15% outpaced reported revenue growth of 28%.
claims.note: Contradicts the release's own figures: 15% expense growth is well below the 28% reported revenue growth, so expenses did not outpace revenue.

claims.claim: Noninterest expense growth of 15% tracked closely with managed revenue growth of 27%.
claims.note: Contradicted by the release: 15% versus 27% is a 12-point gap, not close tracking. The release makes no such comparison.

claims.claim: The release attributes the expense increase to higher compensation and technology costs.
CCB Card Services net charge-offs were $2.2 billion, up $70 million year over year.
claims.note: The $2.2 billion, up $70 million, is CCB segment-wide net charge-offs; the release gives no dollar figure for Card Services net charge-offs, only the 3.34% rate.

claims.claim: The release notes the CCB net charge-off increase was predominantly driven by Card Services.
A substantial portion of reported earnings, $5.6 billion, came from non-recurring gains related to Visa and equity investments.
claims.note: Requires summing $4.6B and $1.0B, a total the release never shows, and presents pre-tax gains as earnings. The release states the earnings impact was $4.2 billion after tax ($21.2B to $16.9B). The release labels these 'significant items,' not non-recurring.
